content.jointProblem: Can an uncertainty-aware spatial linkage pipeline connect farm policies and parcels to available hail estimates and improve identification of potentially underpriced exposure relative to municipality-level rating? The first experiment would audit policy-to-parcel matches and weather resolution, then test whether cadastral spatial-processing methods transfer to this task using held-out storms or years, without assuming that five-kilometre daily weather data can resolve field-level hail intensity.

rationale.text: Lalić has directly relevant experience in cadastral spatial queries and overlays, providing a foundation for linking policy locations, parcels and weather grids.

sources.quote: Query response times were measured across six spatial query types (bounding-box, point-in-polygon, distance, k-nearest-neighbour, clip, and overlay)

rationale.text: His work includes Python and PostGIS preprocessing to detect cadastral geometry errors that could otherwise corrupt policy-to-parcel spatial matches.

sources.quote: This paper presents a preprocessing workflow implemented in Python using Shapely and PostGIS that automatically detects and classifies four error types

rationale.text: His project experience covers coordinate precision, topology correction and production-scale municipal datasets, relevant to building a reliable spatial data pipeline rather than only a map demonstration.

sources.quote: The project developed a reference pipeline covering topological error correction, coordinate precision normalisation, spatial grid partitioning, and incremental tile cache management.
A shared test environment was established at the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad, hosting production-scale datasets from two Hungarian and three Serbian municipalities.

rationale.text: A joint project is consistent with his stated openness to spatial database contract research and his prior industry consulting on PostGIS schema redesign.

sources.quote: contract research on spatial database performance tuning
Lalić provided technical consulting to a Novi Sad-based surveying software company, GeoNS d.o.o., on PostGIS schema redesign for their cadastral data management product

constraints.text: Field-level exposure estimates must preserve uncertainty from both coarse weather observations and settlement-only addresses; precise spatial joins cannot by themselves supply missing hail detail or farm coordinates.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Validation must accommodate the limited historical sample and avoid treating policies affected by the same storm as independent evidence.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: The deliverable must support automated pricing inputs and fit the existing Python batch workflow, rather than stop at a manual GIS overlay.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Implementation and handover must fit the company's shared operational staffing; dedicated internal research capacity cannot be assumed.

sources.quote: The company has no dedicated research unit
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Scheduling must respect the group's stated capacity for only one additional contract engagement from mid-2026 onward; actual availability still needs confirmation.

sources.quote: His group has capacity to take on one additional contract research engagement from mid-2026 onward.

constraints.text: The data-access plan should accommodate his preference for authentic, anonymised production data under NDA, rather than rely only on synthetic examples.

sources.quote: Lalić is interested primarily in collaborations that involve real production cadastral or land-use datasets rather than purely synthetic benchmarks.
He prefers industry partners who can share anonymised but authentic data under NDA.

risks: The strongest evidence concerns cadastral engineering, not hail-intensity reconstruction or actuarial pricing. Transfer to weather–insurance linkage is unvalidated and must be tested in the first experiment; meteorological and actuarial support may be needed.
Daily five-kilometre grids may not contain enough information to distinguish neighbouring farms, even after policy geocoding improves.
Geo-tagged losses may not resolve locations for the wider insured portfolio. Parcel identifiers, boundary access and reliable address-to-parcel matches remain unknown.
Three years of claims may be dominated by a few storms. The reported 18% excess does not establish exposure mapping as its cause; insured values, coverage and claims costs could also contribute.
Production integration could stall: the company's previous flood-risk mapping prototype was completed but has not been integrated into pricing.
Actual researcher availability, company budget, delivery deadline, data permissions and deployment resources are unknown.
questions: Can Lalić confirm availability for this joint project, its earliest start date and the staff time available within the stated one-engagement capacity?
What budget, delivery deadline and named pricing and IT owners can the company commit?

Do policy records contain parcel identifiers, building coordinates or field boundaries, and can these be obtained legally for settlement-only addresses? Are loss geotags claim-site coordinates or settlement centroids?
Does the dataset include all insured policies, including those without claims, together with coverage periods, sums insured, deductibles, premiums and claim dates?
Which MeteoVoj variables actually measure or proxy hail, what are their uncertainty and timestamp conventions, and are radar, storm tracks or independent field observations available for validation?
Can authentic policy, loss and parcel data be shared under NDA with useful spatial precision retained after anonymisation, and what restrictions govern weather-data reuse?
Who will provide meteorological and actuarial expertise, and what held-out evaluation and uncertainty thresholds would justify progressing beyond the first experiment?
What production interfaces, software versions, compute resources and approval requirements must the pipeline satisfy, and who will maintain it after handover?
